source_review.notes: Checked current official Protocol Buffers, Avro, Arrow, Spark, Flink, and Python documentation plus the standards-track CBOR and JSON RFCs. Sources support encoding, framing, schema resolution/evolution, deterministic-encoding limits, application-scoped serializers, state migration, unsafe object decoding, parser limits, and resource-exhaustion claims. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed writer and reader domains, encoder/decoder mappings, semantic projection, frame concatenation, acceptance predicate, wire/payload/logical sizes, compression ratio, batch overhead, and deterministic/cross-version canonicalization notation.
Checked domains, partial error result, compatibility direction, length bounds, and equality qualification.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Semantic equality, byte equality, backward compatibility, forward compatibility, integrity, and authenticity remain distinct.

evidence: Executed bounded-worker-frame with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced a 41-byte frame, 25-byte payload, both reader/writer projections, canonical equality, corruption rejection, and oversized-header rejection.
Recomputed the batching exercise as 4,900,000,000 bytes for individual frames, 4,010,000,000 bytes before batch compression, and 1,604,000,000 bytes at 40 percent.
Checked the fixture header as 4 magic bytes plus one version, one flags byte, two length bytes, and eight digest bytes equals 16 bytes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture sizes are exact for the instructional tag-length-value encoder; they do not predict production codec throughput or security.

evidence: Derived same-schema round trip as identity and evolving-schema round trip as a documented writer-to-reader projection.
Separated deterministic equality within one configuration from the stronger cross-version byte-stability requirement.
Derived acceptance as a conjunction of framing, version, schema, bounds, completeness, integrity, decoding, and application-invariant checks.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Unsupported values and policy limit violations are excluded from the supported round-trip domain rather than silently coerced.

evidence: Reviewed empty, one, maximum, and over-limit frames; truncation; forged lengths; unknown tags; missing/null/default values; integer extremes; float NaNs; Unicode; time units; decimals; maps; and duplicate keys.
Reviewed old/new writers and readers, retained state, rollback, registration drift, lost unknown fields, stale schemas, cross-language keys, partial migration, and executor replacement.

Reviewed hostile object graphs, arbitrary-code deserialization, deep nesting, allocation and decompression bombs, checksum replacement, replay, header substitution, malformed diagnostics, and compromised internal workers.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Wire, expanded, collection, depth, time, and trust boundaries are all explicit.

evidence: Traced framing, immutable schema identity, compatibility, field semantics, bounded allocation, accepted attempt generation, integrity, application validation, and retained evidence through exposition and exercises.
Checked that timestamps, decimals, strings, keys, defaults, unknown fields, and hash inputs require explicit semantics across languages and versions.
Checked that authentication, encryption, checksums, transport protection, and domain validation do not substitute for one another.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not infer semantic compatibility from type decoding or production safety from a happy-path round trip.

evidence: Reviewed all ten serialization-boundary obligations from lifetime classification through evidence and domain review.

Checked counterexamples for codec-equals-protocol, decode-equals-meaning, backward-equals-rolling, default-equals-history, deterministic-equals-stable, checksum-equals-authentication, wire-limit-equals-expanded-limit, and zero-copy-equals-no-work claims.
Reviewed envelope validation order, compatibility matrix, schema migration, key encoding, bounded parsing, authenticated context, and benchmark arguments.
proof_review.notes: Definitional, compatibility, security, empirical, recovery, and consequence evidence are separated.

evidence: Audited uses of requires, must, every, exact, supported, compatible, deterministic, safe, secure, and proof.
Confirmed the fixture is labeled instructional, its truncated digest is not presented as production integrity, and its evidence is not presented as a benchmark.

evidence: Reviewed source retrieval dates, fixture scope, golden/cross-language requirements, fuzz/malformed corpora, migration drills, benchmark dimensions, and tail metrics.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed value models, wire encoding, framing, schema identity/resolution, evolution, determinism, integrity, trust, row/columnar representation, batching, compression, and evidence as one coherent boundary model.
